Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate with a matched 40 fps cap gives a smooth, tear-free experience that the Deck can sustain through most of Acts 1 and 2; render at 1024x640 with FSR to keep GPU load in check while preserving visual quality. Drop Shadow Quality to Low if Act 3 causes sustained dips.

profiles.Summary: Baldur's Gate 3 is a demanding RPG that runs on the Steam Deck with some effort — expect 30–40 fps at low-to-medium settings with FSR upscaling, though CPU-heavy scenes like large battles and cutscenes can cause dips. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support and runs well under Proton, though it pushes the hardware near its limits in Act 2 and 3 areas.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (the Deck's GPU sits between the minimum GTX 970 and recommended RTX 2060 Super) and the Deck hardware profile. On your first run, check fps in a busy outdoor area and in Act 3 city streets — those are the most demanding zones — and drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile if frame rates are unstable.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to relieve GPU pressure; the 9 W TDP and 900 MHz GPU clock cap keep heat and power draw low. Expect occasional dips below 30 in Act 3 city areas even at these settings.

KnownIssues: Frame rate can drop noticeably in Act 2 (Shadow-Cursed Lands) and Act 3 (Baldur's Gate city) due to dense geometry and lighting
Long loading screens between areas are common on the Deck's slower internal storage
Cutscenes and dialogue scenes with many characters can cause CPU-related stuttering
The game's launcher may occasionally appear on first launch — set launch options to skip it if needed

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running uncapped at native 1280x800 with no TDP limit extracts the most from the hardware, but 60 fps is not consistently achievable — expect 40–55 fps with drops in demanding scenes. This profile is best for exploration and dialogue-heavy play; consider switching to Optimal during large combat encounters.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a 40 fps cap gives buttery-smooth pacing that suits BG3's turn-based and exploration gameplay; FSR from 1024x640 keeps the image sharp enough on the OLED. Reduce Shadow Quality to Low in Act 3 if frame rate dips.

profiles.Summary: Baldur's Gate 3 is a demanding RPG that runs on the Steam Deck with Verified status, though its recommended PC specs far exceed the Deck's GPU; expect 30–45 fps with careful settings tuning. The game has native full controller support and plays well on the OLED screen, but busy outdoor areas and Act 2/3 scenes can stress the hardware significantly.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GPU roughly GTX 1050 Ti class vs. recommended RTX 2060 Super), the Steam Deck hardware spec, and general knowledge of BG3's engine demands. On first run, check fps in an outdoor area of Act 1 and in the first city hub — if it struggles to hold 40 fps at Optimal settings, drop to Max Battery or reduce Shadow Quality to Low.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping render resolution to 960x600 with FSR upscaling and capping TDP at 8 W maximises battery; the 30 fps cap smooths frame pacing. Later acts may dip below 30 occasionally even at these settings.

KnownIssues: Performance degrades noticeably in later acts (Act 2 and Act 3 cities) compared to Act 1
Long load times due to the game's large asset sizes; an NVMe SSD helps considerably
Occasional stutters during cutscenes or when entering new areas as assets stream in
Multiplayer/co-op sessions may have additional frame rate instability on Deck

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapped TDP and max GPU clock push the Deck as hard as possible; expect 50+ fps in interiors and turn-based combat, but outdoor scenes and Act 3 can drop to the low 40s. Battery life is short — best used while plugged in.
